title: Future
subtitle: gaan + infinitive, zullen and the present tense with a time word

explain.text: Dutch has no real future tense. For **plans and things that are about to happen** use **gaan + infinitive**. *Gaan* is the conjugated verb (second place) and the infinitive goes to the **end**: *Ik ga morgen koken.* *Wij gaan volgend jaar verhuizen.*

explain.nl: Wat ga je dit weekend doen?
explain.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

explain.nl: Ik ga morgen mijn oma bezoeken.
explain.en: Tomorrow I am going to visit my grandmother.

explain.text: *Gaan* alone means *to go*: *Ik ga naar huis.* With a second verb it means *going to*: *Ik ga eten.*

items.en: I am going to cook tonight.

items.text: Anna ___ volgende week haar oma bezoeken. (gaan)
items.en: Anna is going to visit her grandmother next week.
Are you going to work tomorrow?
items.explain: After jij the t of gaat disappears.

items.en: We are going to buy a house.

explain.text: **Zullen** is used for **promises** (*Ik zal je helpen*), **predictions** (*Het zal morgen regenen*) and **formal** announcements (*Wij zullen u zo snel mogelijk bellen*). With **we** it makes a **suggestion**: *Zullen we gaan?* (Shall we go?)
In everyday speech people often just use the **present tense with a time word**: *Morgen werk ik de hele dag.* *Volgende week gaan wij naar Spanje.* The time word tells you it is the future.
When a time word comes first, the verb follows it: *Morgen werk ik*, not *Morgen ik werk*.

items.q: Wij ___ u zo snel mogelijk bellen.

items.en: Shall we eat together tonight?
I will certainly help you.
Tomorrow it will rain.
Will you come tomorrow?
Next week we are going to Spain.
Tomorrow I will work all day.
items.explain: The time word is first, so the verb follows it and ik comes after.
